name: What room addition permits are needed in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What permits are needed for a room addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood?
mainEntity.text: What permits are needed for a room addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood?

acceptedAnswer.text: A room addition typically requires more than one approval step. At minimum, most projects need building permits and plan review, and many also need structural calculations if the foundation, roof, or load-bearing walls change. Electrical, plumbing, and mechanical work usually need their own permit scope as well. If the addition changes the home’s footprint, height, or lot coverage, zoning review can become a major part of the process. Older homes may also trigger additional review if existing conditions do not match current code or records. Homeowners should expect permit timing to affect the schedule and should have plans prepared before pricing the project, because permit-related redesigns can add cost and delay. The fastest path is to verify feasibility first, then design, then submit for permit rather than building a budget around a rough concept.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most room additions need building permits, and many also require plan check, structural review, and separate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical approvals. In Los Angeles-area cities, permit requirements depend on the size of the addition, whether walls or foundations change, and whether the project affects setbacks, height, or zoning.
